additional_info.subject: Issue Description
additional_info.body:
Just to clarify.
So DC1 has 3 times 40kW, Same as DC2, The groups DC3 and DC4 has 2 times 40kW.
1 Vehicle connected and the EV asks for more then 120 kW then DC1 and DC2 will operate.
But then when a second vehicle is plugged in, the max power is 160kW am I right?
Is it possible when a second vehicle is plugged in that the system downgrades vehicle 1 from DC1 and DC2 to DC1 and DC3 so vehicle 2 also has the possibility of a group of 120 kW combined with a group of 80 kw. So both get 200?
We have had several trucks at the charger, but the second one isn’t charging above 120kW. See picture.
Links to case: ID0426236

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0434039-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / S5 170003680] Second vehicle not charging above 120kw CRM:02919000043
additional_info.body:
Dear Team
,
Hope you are doing well.
Here’s how the dynamic power allocation works for the charger with one EV connected:
The charger has four groups of power converters: DC1, DC2, DC3, and DC4.
DC1 and DC2 each have 3 converters, and each converter provides 40 kW, so each of these groups can supply up to 120 kW.
DC3 and DC4 each have 2 converters, so they can supply up to 80 kW per group (2 × 40 kW).
When the EV requests power:
If the EV requests 120 kW or less, only the DC1 converters operate (up to 3 × 40 kW = 120 kW).
If the EV requests more than 120 kW, then both DC1 and DC2 converters will operate together to supply up to 240 kW.
This setup allows the charger to dynamically allocate power by turning on the appropriate converter groups based on the EV’s power demand.
We have analyzed the logs, and I will explain this using the examples you provided the timestamp::
2025-06-17T10:08:29|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=280|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=300|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=190.9|
EVSE_NowCur[A]=257
|EVSE_NowVol[V]=742.4|
EV_TarCur[A]=256
|EV_TarVol[V]=750|EV_SOC[%]=90
2025-06-17T10:51:13|DC2: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=120|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=177|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=119.3|
EVSE_NowCur[A]=176
|EVSE_NowVol[V]=679|
EV_TarCur[A]=176
|EV_TarVol[V]=697|EV_SOC[%]=41
As you can see in this log, what matters here is that the
EV_TarCur[A]
matches the
EVSE_NowCur[A]
as much as possible.
So, what is happening here?
The EV (vehicle) is requesting the charger to provide 256 amperes & 176 amperes respectively on both outlets DC1 & DC2, in accordance with ISO and DIN standards. The EVSE (charger) will attempt to supply as much current as possible.
Additionally, if there was any issue during the charging session, it would be reflected in the logs, but we could not find anything in the logs regarding this.
If you have any further query, please let us know.
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0434039-DC/Si-D/NL-[MP / S5 170003680] Second vehicle not charging above 120kw CRM:02919000043
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon,
Thank you for your response to our previous email.
I believe there may be a misunderstanding between us. We do indeed understand how the charger's power is currently distributed; the question is whether this distribution can be adjusted.
In practice, we are seeing situations where the first Volvo truck charges at 225kW, while the next vehicle only receives 120kW. We believe it would be better for our customers if both vehicles could receive 200kW.
With the current setup, the first vehicle charges for one hour, while the second takes twice as long.
If both vehicles receive equal power, everyone would be satisfied.
We will soon connect a dispenser to this charging station as well. If the power continues to be distributed in this way, the dispenser won’t be of much use to us.
Ideally, we would like to see the following configuration:
Vehicle 1 receives 200kW
Vehicle 2 receives 200kW
Is this possible through a setting?
We look forward to your response.
Met vriendelijke groet
Luuk Laponder
Accountmanager E-Mobility
